title: ISE RADIUS Change-of-Authorization (CoA) Failure Detection
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'ISE RADIUS Change-of-Authorization (CoA) Failure Detection' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `network_ise_radius_change_of_authorization_coa_failure_d` (UC-17.1.56), SOC dashboard panel "Network — ISE RADIUS Change-of-Authorization (CoA) Failure Detection", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:network_controls.

compliance.controlObjective: Incident-response closure evidence for change-of-authorization workflows.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=nac` sourcetype='cisco:ise:syslog' that satisfy the UC-17.1.56 SPL filters for 'ISE RADIUS Change-of-Authorization (CoA) Failure Detection'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `nac` / `cisco:ise:syslog` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `network_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-17.1.56.

dataSources: ISE syslog `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog` *Authentication* category — CoA codes `5417` (CoA initiated), `5418` (CoA succeeded), `5419` (CoA failed), `5420` (CoA timeout), `5421` (CoA NAS not responding). Fields: `coa_action` (port-bounce|port-shutdown|reauth|disconnect), `NAS-IP-Address`, `endpoint_mac`, `error_code`. NAD-side: `index=network sourcetype=cisco:ios` `%RADIUS-3-COA_NACK`. CIM mapping: `Change.action`.
app: `Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)) + Cisco network TA.
spl:
(index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode IN (5417, 5419, 5420, 5421))
  OR (index=network sourcetype="cisco:ios" "%RADIUS-3-COA")
| eval action = case(MessageCode=="5417", "initiated", MessageCode=="5419", "failed", MessageCode=="5420", "timeout", MessageCode=="5421", "nas_no_response", like(_raw, "%COA_NACK%"), "nas_nack")
| stats count by NAS-IP-Address, action, coa_action
| where action != "initiated" AND count > 5
description: Detects RADIUS CoA failures, timeouts, and NAS no-response events at scale. CoA is how ISE pushes runtime authorization changes (quarantine, reauth, port-bounce) to NADs — failures mean the enforcement action didn't reach the device.
value: When SOAR pushes a quarantine to ISE and ISE pushes a CoA to the NAD that fails, the endpoint *remains uncontained*. CoA failure detection is the closure validation for incident-response automation.
implementation: Confirm *Authentication* category at INFO. Schedule every 5 min, search window `-15m@m to @m`, throttle suppression on `NAS-IP-Address` for 30 min.
visualization: (1) Single value: CoA failures last 1h. (2) Top-N NADs by failure count. (3) Failure-class breakdown.

references.title: RFC 5176 — Dynamic Authorization Extensions to RADIUS

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Certificate or EAP profile rollout** — Clients fail EAP-TLS during staged cert deployment for 'ISE RADIUS Change-of-Authorization (CoA) Failure Detection'. Cross-check `FailureReason` and CMDB cert expiry.

2. **RADIUS/PSN maintenance restart** — Short auth failure burst while ISE node restarts. Match change window on `index=changes`.

3. **Guest or IoT onboarding surge** — Legitimate MAC registration spike skews `index=nac` `cisco:ise:syslog` baselines.

4. **Approved pen-test or scanner traffic** — Red-team exercises from netblock in `approved_scanners.csv` mimic auth failures.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `CallingStationID`, `NAS-IP-Address`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• NAD configured with `aaa server radius dynamic-author` (and matching shared secret).
• `nad_inventory.csv` with `nas_ip`, `coa_supported`.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Validate event flow.

Step 2 — Create the search
Search in `spl` field. Schedule every 5 min.

Step 3 — Validate
Provoke as above.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard "ISE — CoA Health":
• Single value: failures last 1h.
• Top-N NADs.
• Failure-class.

Alerting: PagerDuty medium on sustained CoA failure for one NAD.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **Shared-secret mismatch** — Realign on NAD and ISE.
• **NAS no response** — UDP/3799 (or 1700) blocked.
• **CoA initiated but NAD doesn't enforce** — NAD has `aaa authorization network ... default group ...` not configured to honour CoA.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)) + Cisco network TA.). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog, cisco:ios into nac, network. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`NAS-IP-Address, action, coa_action`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: When ISE tells a switch 'kick this person off the network' via a special message, we make sure the switch actually heard the message and acted on it.
